text:
Brayden Schenn is 35, a Stanley Cup winner with St. Louis in 2019, and now a mentor on Long Island; the New York Post wrote about his bond with young Victor Eklund this week. On the ice, he's been better than anyone expected after a replacement-level season by Evolving-Hockey's numbers: 6 goals and 15 points in 19 games, and three points in the 5-2 win in Los Angeles that snapped the Islanders' four-game winless run.

Most of the jump is finishing around him. His points per hour sit at 2.82 against 1.74 last season, his own shooting is 18.8%, and his teammates have scored 6.37 more goals than expected with him on. His own chance rate, 1.04 expected goals per hour, is up only modestly from 0.92.

At five on five, the Islanders have had 47.37% of the expected goals with him on and been a little better without him. He's a dangerous-ice shooter who throws hits (43 already) and, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, gets the puck out cleanly. Watch whether the scoring holds when the bounces stop.
headline: Brayden Schenn, the veteran in the room
